after: ## The nine units and what they measure
alt: Three base units: kilogram for mass, metre for distance and second for time. Six derived units: m/s for speed (distance ÷ time), m/s² for acceleration (change in velocity ÷ time), N for force (mass × acceleration), N/kg for g (weight ÷ mass), and the Physics-only Nm for moment (force × perpendicular distance) and kg m/s for momentum (mass × velocity).
caption: Three base units; the other six are built from them like their equations.

after: ## How the derived units are built
alt: One newton is 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 kg m/s². So N/kg = (kg m/s²)/kg = m/s², which is why g = 10 N/kg and free fall is at 10 m/s². A moment is N × m = Nm, and momentum is kg × m/s = kg m/s, the same as N s.
caption: Since 1 N = 1 kg m/s², N/kg and m/s² are the same unit.

after: ## How the derived units are built
alt: Bars show a velocity u, then u + 3, u + 6, u + 9 and u + 12 m/s after 1, 2, 3 and 4 seconds: an acceleration of 3 m/s² adds 3 m/s to the velocity in each second.
caption: m/s² means the velocity changes by that many m/s every second.

alt: Conversions: 850 g = 0.850 kg, 35 cm = 0.35 m, 12 mm = 0.012 m, 1.6 km = 1600 m, 2.5 min = 150 s, 1.5 h = 5400 s, 90 km/h = 25 m/s and 1.2 tonnes = 1200 kg. 1 km/h = 1000 m ÷ 3600 s, about 0.28 m/s, so km/h values are divided by 3.6.
caption: Everyday units go into kg, m and s before any equation.

after: ## Using units to check an equation
alt: Unit checks. v² = u² + 2as has m²/s² on both sides, so it is consistent. v = u² + 2as has m/s on the left but m²/s² on the right, so it is wrong. F = (mv − mu) ÷ t gives kg m/s ÷ s = kg m/s², a newton. An acceleration in m/s or a moment in N signals a missing step.
caption: Both sides of a correct equation have the same units.

after: ## Worked example 1: a chain of calculations
alt: A 600 g trolley goes from rest to 1.8 m/s in 1.2 s. With m = 0.600 kg: acceleration = 1.8 / 1.2 = 1.5 m/s²; force = 0.600 × 1.5 = 0.90 N; momentum = 0.600 × 1.8 = 1.08, about 1.1 kg m/s. Substituting 600 would give 900 N, a thousand times too large.
caption: Convert the mass once, then each answer carries its own unit.

alt: A spanner 25 cm long with a 40 N force at right angles to its end. Converting 25 cm to 0.25 m, the moment about the nut is 40 × 0.25 = 10 Nm; using 25 directly gives 1000, a value in newton centimetres.
caption: Convert centimetres to metres so the moment comes out in Nm.
